boot.errorText: Check that the server is running and your network is up, then try again.
libstate.listErrorText: The server answered with an error:
libstate.firstRunAdmin: There are no libraries yet. Add your first one: pick the folder with your book archives and its INPX index.
libstate.noLibrariesReader: An administrator has to add a library before there is anything to read. Check back later.
libstate.notFoundText: It may have been deleted, or the link is wrong.
libstate.rebuildingText: Rebuilding the catalog of «{name}» after an update — this takes about a minute. This page continues by itself when it's done.
libstate.importingText: «{name}» is being imported. This page continues by itself when it's done.
libstate.failed: The library could not be imported
libstate.failedAdmin: Fix the cause below (for example a moved INPX file), then retry.
libstate.failedReader: An administrator has to fix this library. Details:

login.adminLogin: Sign in with a local administrator account
login.sso.error.state: The sign-in took too long or was started in another tab. Try again.
login.sso.error.provider: The sign-in provider refused or cancelled the sign-in.
login.sso.error.token: The sign-in provider's answer could not be verified. Ask the administrator to check the server log.
login.sso.error.unavailable: The sign-in provider can't be reached right now. Try again later or use your password.
login.sso.error.not_linked: No freeLib account is linked to this sign-in. Ask an administrator, or sign in with your password and link it in Settings → Account.
login.sso.error.already_linked: This sign-in is already linked to another freeLib account.
login.sso.error.session: You were signed out while linking. Sign in and try again.
login.sso.error.rate_limited: Too many failed sign-ins. Wait a few minutes and try again.
login.sso.error.busy: Too many sign-ins in progress. Try again in a few minutes.
account.sso.title: Single sign-on
account.sso.linked: Linked to your sign-in provider account
account.sso.notLinked: Not linked. Link it to use “{label}” on the login page.
account.sso.unlinkConfirm: Unlink single sign-on from this account? You will sign in with your password.
account.sso.unlinkNeedsPassword: Set a password below before unlinking, or you could not sign in any more.
account.sso.unlinkPasswordOff: Password sign-in is disabled on this server, so single sign-on stays linked.
account.password.title: Password
account.password.hint: Used on the login page and by reading apps (OPDS).
account.password.ssoHint: Your account signs in with single sign-on and has no password. Reading apps that use the OPDS catalog can't do single sign-on: set a password here and use it there with your user name.
account.password.saved: Password saved. Other sessions were signed out.
settings.users.noPasswordHint: Signs in with single sign-on only (no OPDS until a password is set)

ratings.libTooltip: Library rating (from the library index): {n} of 5
ratings.extSource: Average rating of the work on openlibrary.org
tokens.title: API tokens & MCP
tokens.intro: Let AI assistants (Claude and other MCP clients) search your library, see your shelves and ratings, suggest books and send them to your devices. Each client gets its own token; revoke it any time.
tokens.mcpDisabled: The MCP endpoint is disabled by the administrator.
tokens.copyFailed: Could not copy; select the text instead
tokens.name: Token name
tokens.namePlaceholder: e.g. Claude Desktop on my laptop
tokens.scope.read: search the catalog, read my shelves, ratings and history
tokens.scope.send: send books to my devices (Send to Kindle)
tokens.copyNow: Copy your new token now — it will not be shown again.
tokens.hint.desktop: Easiest: add freeLib as a custom connector (above) and sign in. With a token instead, add this to claude_desktop_config.json (Settings → Developer → Edit Config; needs Node.js for mcp-remote) and restart Claude Desktop:
tokens.hint.other: Any client that speaks MCP over Streamable HTTP with custom headers (Cursor, VS Code, …):
tokens.revokeConfirm: Revoke the token "{name}"? Clients using it stop working at once.
tokens.openMode: The server runs without accounts (open mode): tokens belong to the implicit administrator and stop working once accounts are set up.
settings.server.mcpEnabled: Enable the MCP endpoint (/mcp) for AI assistants
settings.server.mcpHint: Users connect by signing in from Claude (Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector; needs FREELIB_PUBLIC_URL with https) or with personal API tokens (Settings → Account).
settings.server.extPrivacy: The server sends book titles and author surnames of your libraries to openlibrary.org (about one request a second, in the background) — nothing about users. Turn it off to send nothing.
settings.server.extCounts: {looked} of {total} books looked up · {found} found · {rated} with ratings
settings.server.extContact: Tip: set FREELIB_CONTACT_EMAIL so Open Library can reach you about your requests.
libraries.extProgress: Open Library: {looked} of {total} looked up, {found} found
libraries.extHint: Ratings are looked up in the background, about one book a second
settings.devices.orderHint: Drag the handle or use the arrows to order your devices. The first one is your default: the quick send button, the Send dialog and AI assistants (MCP) use it. The order is yours only.
settings.devices.defaultHint: Your default device (first in the list)
oauth.error.invalid_client: The app that sent you here is unknown to this server or not trusted. Start the connection again from the app; the administrator can trust more app hosts with FREELIB_OAUTH_CLIENT_HOSTS.
oauth.error.invalid_redirect_uri: The app asked to return to an address it did not register. For your safety you were not sent there.
oauth.error.invalid_request: The authorization request is incomplete or malformed.
oauth.error.disabled: Connecting apps by signing in is off on this server: the administrator must set FREELIB_PUBLIC_URL to its https:// address.
oauth.error.rate_limited: Too many connection attempts. Wait a minute and start again from the app.
oauth.error.generic: This connection request cannot be used. Start again from the app.
oauth.unverified: The app named itself; this name is not verified
oauth.redirectTo: You will be sent back to
oauth.loopback: This app runs on your own computer. Only allow it if you just started this connection yourself (for example in Claude Code).
oauth.openMode: The server runs without accounts (open mode): the app acts as the administrator while open mode lasts.
oauth.revokeHint: You can revoke access at any time in Settings → Account → API tokens & MCP.
oauthApps.step1: In claude.ai or Claude Desktop open Settings → Connectors and choose "Add custom connector".
oauthApps.step2: Name it freeLib and enter the URL
oauthApps.step3: Click Connect, sign in here and allow access. No token to copy.
oauthApps.codeHint: Claude Code: run this, then /mcp to sign in:
oauthApps.off: Signing in from claude.ai or Claude Desktop needs the administrator to set FREELIB_PUBLIC_URL to this server's https:// address. Until then, use a personal token below.
oauthApps.title: Authorized apps
oauthApps.none: No apps connected by signing in.
oauthApps.revokeConfirm: Revoke access of "{name}"? It stops working at once and must be connected again.
tokens.personalHint: For clients without sign-in support, scripts, or when the server has no public https address.
